summary.text: An 87-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus, depression, hypertension and hyperlipidemia presented after outpatient laboratory results showed anemia with hemoglobin 6.8 g/dL. She was independent at home and reported no chest pain, shortness of breath, palpitations, dizziness, syncope or leg swelling. Examination showed conjunctival pallor and a crescendo-decrescendo murmur at the right upper sternal border radiating to the carotids.

Endoscopy showed gastric antral and distal duodenal bulb angiovascular malformations treated with thermal therapy; colonoscopy was unremarkable. Echocardiography showed moderate-to-severe aortic stenosis, cardiac catheterization minimal-to-mild coronary irregularities, and von Willebrand factor antigen was decreased with a positive ristocetin cofactor test, supporting acquired von Willebrand disease. Ferritin was low and reticulocytes elevated.

She was transfused and started on octreotide. New-onset atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular rate was managed with fluids, transfusions, metoprolol and then digoxin, and she was not considered a candidate for anticoagulation because of ongoing bleeding. Surgical risk was assessed and TAVR was recommended over open replacement, but she declined all invasive and minimally invasive interventions and elected conservative care.

Octreotide, moved from intravenous to subcutaneous, controlled the gastrointestinal bleeding without further transfusions. Hemoglobin rose from 6.6 g/dL on admission to 8.6 g/dL at discharge after six units of packed red blood cells, intravenous ferric gluconate and oral ferrous sulfate. She became deconditioned, was discharged to home hospice, and died 2 months after discharge.
